title: Professional Python Project Companion
text:
A professional Python project includes more than good source code. It includes the files, conventions, automation, documentation, and validation that allow the project to be developed, maintained, and shared reliably.
This companion explains those parts.
It presents one coherent and intentionally opinionated approach to professional Python project infrastructure. The particular tools and configurations are chosen for their popularity and longevity, but like everything, can be expected to evolve. The engineering concerns of consistency, reproducibility, validation, collaboration, documentation, and maintenance that they address will remain.
Maintained canonical examples are included and may be forked, adapted, and evolved for other projects, teams, and organizations.

title: 2  Preface
text:
This is a concise guide to selected infrastructure for a professional Python project.
The companion is intentionally opinionated. Professional projects require concrete engineering decisions. Examples reflect choices I find valuable enough to use across professionally maintained Python repositories.
Like everything in our rapidly-changing field, choices will evolve.
Readers are encouraged to understand the reasoning, adopt what serves their work, and create their own project standards.

title: 13  .editorconfig
text:
13.1 Purpose
.editorconfig defines basic text-file conventions that compatible editors apply automatically.
It helps contributors using different editors and operating systems produce files with consistent indentation, encoding, line endings, and final-newline behavior.

title: 13  .editorconfig
text:
13.2 Maintenance
Change .editorconfig when the project adopts different text conventions or begins using file types that require different settings.
Most projects rarely need to modify it after the initial decisions have been made.
